page: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance designed for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM allocations relative to compute capacity. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It is provisioned with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU, along with 928 GB of local SSD temporary storage. The underlying x86_64 processor includes hardware acceleration flags such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions and dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results characterize the instance as particularly robust in memory handling and single-core compute tasks. It achieved strong top-quartile results in PassMark memory testing (2,848.4) and stress-ng single-core processing (2,904.58), alongside solid image processing performance. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 77.97 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 44.59 GB/sec for uncached writes. General multi-threaded tasks, including Geekbench multi-core execution (14,309.0) and PassMark CPU evaluation (35,490.08), settled squarely in the middle 50% distribution. In-memory data throughput reached 27.77 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

The primary operational tradeoff of the E64-32as_v4 stems from its constrained core count relative to its memory footprint. While instances in the standard E64 family deploy 64 vCPUs, this constrained-core variant caps compute at 32 vCPUs to optimize per-core software licensing costs. Highly parallel computational jobs and large-scale model inference, such as 70B parameter LLM processing, are limited by the vCPU count and the absence of hardware accelerators.

The E64-32as_v4 is best suited for large enterprise relational databases, in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, data warehousing engines, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines where licensing models penalize high CPU core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive applications requiring high memory-to-vCPU ratios. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, the configuration delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 512.0 GB of RAM, and 928 GB of local SSD temporary storage without GPU acceleration. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in memory evaluation metrics and single-core compute benchmarks, backed by memory bandwidth reaching 77.97 GB/sec on uncached reads. Throughput testing shows 27.77 million Redis SET operations per second and standard multi-core processing efficiency. By constraining compute resources to 32 vCPUs while retaining a 512 GB memory pool, this instance offers licensing cost advantages for software charged on a per-core basis. It is optimal for large relational databases, in-memory caches, and memory-heavy analytics workloads.
